forbidden.name: no-circular
forbidden.comment: No circular dependencies anywhere in the CLI.

forbidden.name: services-never-import-acts
forbidden.comment: Services are adapter-agnostic business logic — they must not know about command handlers.

forbidden.name: services-only-adapter-ports
forbidden.comment: Services may depend on adapter PORT interfaces only, never concrete node-*/exec-*/system-* implementations or fakes.

forbidden.name: services-ports-type-only
forbidden.comment: Port imports from services must be type-only (the kernel injects the implementation).

forbidden.name: dd-core-never-imports-output
forbidden.comment: dd-core returns structured values and never imports harness envelopes or exits.

forbidden.name: dd-core-never-imports-acts
forbidden.comment: dd-core is a library boundary and never imports command handlers.

forbidden.name: dd-core-never-imports-node-adapters
forbidden.comment: dd-core is ports-free and never imports any harness adapter.

forbidden.name: dd-graph-never-imports-render
forbidden.comment: dd graph emits mermaid directly. A renderer import anywhere in its chain would re-couple the render and links phases, which were split so they could land in parallel.

forbidden.name: dd-links-never-imports-render
forbidden.comment: The links layer consumes the render layer only through an injected interface; it never imports it.

forbidden.name: dd-links-never-imports-output
forbidden.comment: The links layer returns structured findings and never imports harness envelopes or exits.

forbidden.name: dd-links-never-imports-acts
forbidden.comment: The links layer is a library boundary and never imports command handlers.

forbidden.name: dd-mutate-never-imports-output
forbidden.comment: The dd writer layer returns structured refusals and never imports harness envelopes or exits — the act maps a refusal reason to an E-code, exactly as it does for dd-core and links.

forbidden.name: dd-mutate-never-imports-acts
forbidden.comment: The dd writer layer is a library boundary and never imports command handlers.

forbidden.name: dd-mutate-never-imports-node-adapters
forbidden.comment: The dd writer layer is `(doc, address, value) => doc | refusal`. Reading and writing files belongs to the act, so a mutation is testable — and a refusal provable — without a filesystem.

forbidden.name: dd-plan-never-imports-output
forbidden.comment: The plan semantic layer returns structured findings and never imports harness envelopes or exits — the act maps a finding class to an E-code, exactly as every other dd layer does.

forbidden.name: dd-plan-never-imports-acts
forbidden.comment: The plan semantic layer is a library boundary and never imports command handlers.

forbidden.name: dd-plan-never-imports-node-adapters
forbidden.comment: The plan semantic layer takes already-loaded documents and already-walked edges. Reading files belongs to the act, so a contradiction is provable without a filesystem.

forbidden.name: dd-plan-never-imports-render
forbidden.comment: The plan semantic layer reads structure, never markdown — the same boundary that keeps dd graph independent of the renderer.

forbidden.name: dd-render-never-imports-output
forbidden.comment: The dd renderer is pure — it returns markdown and never imports harness envelopes or exits.

forbidden.name: dd-render-never-imports-acts
forbidden.comment: The dd renderer is a library boundary and never imports command handlers.

forbidden.name: dd-render-never-imports-node-adapters
forbidden.comment: The dd renderer takes precomputed inputs — it is ports-free and imports no harness adapter.

forbidden.name: flow-consumes-dd-sdk-only
forbidden.comment: The flow spine is an EXTERNAL consumer of dd, not a co-resident: it may import ONLY dd's published SDK barrels (services/dd/links/index.ts, services/dd/schema/index.ts and services/dd/plan/index.ts), never a dd module path. That line is the whole difference between an SDK and a shared folder. When the flow needs something dd does not export, EXPOSE a named seam on a barrel deliberately (as `deriveSchemaItems` was, and as `readPlanCheck` is for the check-kind gate) — never reach past one. Covers TYPE-ONLY imports too (see tsPreCompilationDeps above): a type reaching past the barrel couples the flow to an internal shape just as hard as a value does, and breaks the same way when dd moves it.

forbidden.name: adapters-stay-leaf
forbidden.comment: Adapters are leaves — they never import services, acts, or output.

forbidden.name: output-stays-leaf
forbidden.comment: The output/envelope layer must not reach back into services or acts.

forbidden.name: no-fakes-in-prod
forbidden.comment: Fake adapters are test doubles — production source must not import them.
